rule.title: Rules check
rule.official: The Controller of Budget found that counties together spent {wages} of total revenue on wages, above the {limit} limit, and that some counties did not pay their full wage bill, which makes their ratios look lower. Below is our own check for this county, using the same method.

rule.development.line: Share of the {fy} budget for development in {name}. The minimum is {limit}.
rule.development.law: The law: "over the medium term a minimum of thirty percent of the county government's budget shall be allocated to the development expenditure". This shows one year, and the rule looks across several, so one year alone does not settle it.
rule.wages.q: How much of its revenue went on wages?
rule.wages.line: Wages and benefits as a share of total revenue in {name}, {fy}. The limit is {limit}.
rule.wages.law: The law: the limit "shall not exceed thirty five (35) percent of the county government's total revenue", leaving out revenue from extractive natural resources such as oil and coal. Revenue here is what the county reported, including money carried forward, as in the Controller of Budget's own ratios.

methods.title: Methods
methods.line: Every number we work out ourselves, and how. Each is tagged "Our calculation" where it appears, and each has a test.
methods.never: We never estimate, interpolate or scale a missing figure. A figure we do not have shows as not loaded.
methods.gross.how: Supply plus Appropriations-in-Aid, recurrent and development, as the Appropriation Act prints them. This is the gross amount.
methods.sector.how: The sum of its votes. Which votes are in each sector comes from the Parliamentary Budget Office's tables, not from our judgment.
methods.change.how: (this year minus last year) divided by last year, times 100. Approved against approved, in cash terms, adding the same votes in both years.
methods.stages.how: Figures of different stages are shown side by side, never added, and no change is worked out between them.
methods.hundred.how: A part divided by total spending, times 100, rounded to whole shillings. Below KSh 1 it is given in cents, and below 10 cents as "under 10 cents".
methods.absorption.how: Development money spent divided by the development budget, times 100, as the Controller of Budget prints it. We recompute each printed percentage from the amounts.
methods.wages.how: A county's wages divided by its total revenue, times 100. Our division must reproduce every ratio the Controller of Budget names, or the build stops.
methods.rules.how: A county's share compared with the limit in the law: wages at most 35% of revenue, development at least 30%. The report's own finding comes first, and the law is quoted.
methods.projects.how: Two rules, from the Development Estimates alone: money last year and none this year; and one specific name under more than one vote. Each gives a question, never a finding.
methods.taxes.how: Your amount times each part's share of spending, in whole shillings. Leftover shillings go to the largest remainders, so the parts add back to your amount.
methods.days.how: Whole days from today in Nairobi to the date the law fixes, worked out again in your browser.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.line: The words this site uses, in plain language, with their Kiswahili.
term.vote.def: A ministry, state department or agency that Parliament gives money to in the Appropriation Act.
term.programme.def: A part of a vote's work with its own money, aim and targets, such as Road Transport.
term.supply.def: Money a vote gets from the Exchequer, the national government's main account.
term.aia.def: Money an agency raises itself, such as fees, and is allowed to spend. Supply plus Appropriations-in-Aid is the gross amount.
term.recurrent.def: The running costs of government: salaries, operations and transfers.
term.development.def: Money for building things that last, such as roads, clinics and water projects.
term.cfs.def: Spending paid before anything else, mostly interest on public debt and pensions. It is not in any ministry's vote.
term.bps.def: The National Treasury's statement of the year's priorities and spending ceilings, due in Parliament by 15 February.
term.absorption.def: The share of the development budget actually spent in a year, as the Controller of Budget reports it.
term.payables.def: Amounts owed for goods, services and works already delivered but not yet paid.
term.osr.def: Money a county raises itself, such as rates, licences and fees.
term.ngcdf.def: The National Government Constituencies Development Fund: national money run by constituency committees, never part of county money.
term.release.def: A dated snapshot of every figure on this site. Citing the release lets anyone find the exact number you used.
